analysis: Examined .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py (CI threat-review tooling tests, not provider/coordinator runtime). Changes: imports Scanner and ThreatContext (head lines 12, 15); adds workload call-policy tests (head ~301-341) asserting that no unplanned Bedrock call occurs before plan_calls, that the stage-admitted limit is planned+1 shared repair, that an emergency ceiling (BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS) raises BEDROCK_WORKLOAD_LIMIT before the unadmitted stage, and that invalid policies or ceilings (unlimited, 101, 0) raise ReviewUnavailable without requests or fallback. A WorkloadScanTests case (head ~394-440) exercises a large 31-batch scan with hierarchical integration and one repair, checking clean() passes only on finished complete results. Policy tests (head ~481-499) assert that incomplete finished results require human review and never clear. These are tests only. They do not touch threat-model assets (A-001..A-017) or boundaries TB-002/TB-011, and they add no runtime attack surface. The tested behavior is fail-closed with respect to merge clearance and paid-call expansion. The implementations are outside this batch: threat_review/bedrock.py plan_calls/limit/ceiling and budget_scan Scanner. Integration should confirm that BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY=workload cannot be enabled by untrusted PR input to expand spend, and that the default ceiling is bounded (the test implies a maximum of 100). Missing implementation source is a coverage limit; no regression is identified from the tests themselves.
